title: The origin of democracy: Athenian democracy
competency: Identify the birthplace of democracy and explain the nature, limits and contributions of Athenian democracy.

keywords.def: A Greek city-state; the birthplace of democracy (5th century B.C.).
The direct democracy of Athens, where adult male citizens voted in the Assembly.
A condition in which a person is exploited and denied most democratic rights.

en.text: Democracy is thought to have begun in Athens, a Greek city-state, in the 5th century B.C. Every adult male citizen could vote in the Assembly, so it was direct democracy. Athens gave us direct participation, political equality, government responsible to the people and the idea of citizens.

screens.title: Birthplace
screens.ask: Where do most historians say democracy was born?
screens.after: Democracy is thought to have begun in Athens, a Greek city-state, in the 5th century B.C.

screens.title: 3.2.1 Athenian democracy
paras: Democracy is thought to have begun in the 5th century B.C. in the Greek city-state of Athens.
Athens was not the only democratic Greek city-state. It was the most prominent and powerful.
screens.note: REMEMBER: Athens is the birthplace (origin) of democracy.

screens.title: Direct voting in the Assembly
paras: In Athens, every adult male citizen could vote in the Assembly on important issues.
Citizens voted directly and personally. So Greek democracy was direct.

screens.title: What Athens gave us
items: Citizens voted themselves in the Assembly.
Equal political rights, at least for free adult male citizens.
The idea that government should answer to the people.
Athens invented the idea of citizens.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A Greek city-state; the birthplace of democracy (5th century B.C.).
The direct democracy of Athens, where adult male citizens voted in the Assembly.

screens.text: Why was Athenian democracy called direct?
opts: Citizens voted personally in the Assembly
Citizens elected a parliament every five years
screens.ans: Citizens voted personally in the Assembly
screens.why: Citizens voted directly and personally in the Assembly.
screens.clue: Who did the voting in the Assembly?

screens.text: Athens was the only Greek city-state with a democratic government.
screens.why: Other city-states had democracy too. Athens was the most prominent and powerful.

screens.text: Tap every idea that modern democracy got from Athens.
screens.why: The book lists these four elements we still relate to today.
screens.clue: Slavery and kings are not democratic ideas.

screens.text: Democracy began in the 5th century B.C. About how long ago is that?
screens.why: The 5th century B.C. is the 400s B.C. From about 450 B.C. to today (about A.D. 2025) is about 450 + 2,025 ≈ 2,500 years.
screens.clue: Add the years before Christ to the years after.

en.text: Athenian democracy had serious limits. Only a small part of adults could vote. Women, slaves and foreign residents were not citizens. Many citizens stayed away from meetings, and the system was slow and costly. Still, it was the foundation of modern democracy.

screens.title: Who could vote?
screens.ask: In Athens, could women vote in the Assembly?
opts: No, only adult male citizens voted
screens.after: Only adult male citizens voted. Women, slaves and foreign residents were left out.

screens.title: Flaws of Athenian democracy
paras: Only a small part of the adult population could vote. So it was undemocratic in modern terms.
Citizenship was for males whose parents were both Athenians.
Women, slaves and resident aliens were not citizens.

screens.title: More flaws
paras: Most citizens stayed away from most meetings, even when paid to attend.
It was complicated, time-consuming and costly.
Self-government did not always give clear state policy.
screens.note: Athens is called the birthplace of democracy, but it was not fully democratic. Slavery was widespread.

screens.title: Democracy in Ethiopia today
paras: All citizens should take part in their government. No citizen should be a slave.
All Ethiopian citizens have the right to take part in local and national government without discrimination.
No Ethiopian citizen should be subjected to slavery.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A condition in which a person is exploited and denied most democratic rights.

screens.text: Which group could NOT be citizens in Athens?
screens.why: Citizenship was restricted to a small male elite.
screens.clue: Who was left out of citizenship?

screens.title: Contribution or limitation?
items: Only a small elite were citizens
Political equality for free male citizens
Hard to use in the modern world.
screens.why: Athens gave lasting ideas but also had serious flaws.
screens.clue: Is it something we still use, or a problem?

screens.text: There is no contribution from ancient Athenian democracy to modern democracy.
screens.why: Athens served as a foundation for modern democracy.
screens.clue: Recall the four elements we still relate to.

screens.text: Hiwot says: "Athens was fully democratic because it was the birthplace of democracy." What is the best reply?
opts: No: most adults could not take part and slavery was common
screens.ans: No: most adults could not take part and slavery was common
screens.why: Being the birthplace does not mean being fully democratic. Most Athenians could not take part, and slavery was widespread.
screens.clue: Who was allowed to vote in Athens?

test.text: Democracy is thought to have begun in:
test.why: In the Greek city-state of Athens.

test.text: In Athens, women and slaves could vote in the Assembly.
test.why: Only adult male citizens could vote.

test.text: Which statement about Athenian democracy is true?
opts: Citizenship was restricted to a small elite
Women and slaves were not allowed to participate
It was a direct form of democracy

test.text: Why is Athenian-style direct democracy hard to use in a modern country?
opts: It is complicated, slow and costly, and people prefer to work
test.ans: It is complicated, slow and costly, and people prefer to work
test.why: The book says its relevance today is limited for these reasons.

notes.text: The book says Athenian democracy "was hardly an exercise in lean movement"; probably "lean government" was meant. Taught as: complicated, slow and costly.
The book says lack of bureaucracy led to "infected government"; probably a misprint for "ineffective government". Not used in items.
p.68 says "these two beliefs continue to influence us"; no two beliefs are named nearby (four contributions are listed on p.66). Not used.
The challenge "about 2,500 years ago" is an added estimate (5th century B.C. to today).
